verdictStatement: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. All three equality tests the dispatch names pass by ==: namedCorpusNotAuthored is exact to live G20 v1 at one class and matches the live DR-G20 harness cell; reservedVerbatim is exact to live v4's reserved array at six members in order; and all 13 cited path/digest pairs measure equal with zero mismatches, with recordedInputs.HEAD agreeing with the top-level head and live HEAD as the artifact's own invariant requires. The honesty limb is handled precisely rather than approximately — D-110 records 'Claude observations CLAUDE-V4-O1/O2/O3 travel as honesty work. O-4 is resolved', and the join states both halves, so the fourth observation is dispositioned rather than dropped; the class is typed leftoverDesign false, rideStanding honesty, not SATISFIED, not discharged. OBL-DR125-ACTIVATION is held on DR-118 exactly as live G20 v1's leftoverNameNote words it, and the code is genuinely live in the DR-118 family. The two subjects are CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and bind NOTHING, DR-125 leftover-design is not claimed closed, v4 is not applied, no API, framework or envelope is invented, no D9 or exit value is minted, no DR-G* row is added, required-now is 26, and the subject did not move. I ran seven further refutations of my own — an unclassified reserved member, an overstated D-110 standing, a collapsed row-versus-gate owner, an uncovered acceptance-evidence cell, an unhandled SARIF token, a missing specifiedNotLeftover class, and a minted D9 value — and all seven failed against live bytes. The SARIF probe is worth naming: minting a DR-122 leftover there would have been wrong, because live G20 v1 expressly declines to mint leftover codes for DR-122, and the join disclosing without minting is the correct handling.
